title: NVIDIA RTX 4090 Pricing
summary: Compare RTX 4090 cloud pricing from four providers against the 14-provider median, see who undercuts Beam, and learn when serverless beats an always-on GPU.

# NVIDIA RTX 4090 Pricing


Eli Mernit


September 29, 2026


3 min read


An NVIDIA RTX 4090 costs $0.20 to $0.44 per GPU-hour to rent on demand from the providers below, against a market median of $0.47 across 14 providers. Beam's RTX 4090 machine is $0.44 an hour with vCPU, RAM, and NVMe included. Beam's serverless 4090 bills $0.69 an hour for the GPU, plus CPU and RAM, and scales to zero when idle.


## Key takeaways


- The $0.20 floor is the cheapest single offer on Vast.ai's marketplace. The median Vast.ai offer is $0.48, and nine in ten cost at least $0.40.
- Salad High priority ($0.33) and RunPod Community Cloud ($0.34) are the cheapest fixed rates, both below Beam's $0.44.
- Beam's machine is $0.03 under the market median, and its serverless option pays off for spiky traffic.

## How these prices were collected


Each figure is an on-demand, per-GPU list price for a single-GPU shape where one is offered. Spot and interruptible rates appear only in the notes. Marketplace data from Vast.ai.


- [Vast.ai's GPU pricing page](https://vast.ai/pricing) has the floor and median offers.
- [Salad's pricing page](https://salad.com/pricing/) lists each priority tier.
- [RunPod's pricing page](https://www.runpod.io/pricing) has both cloud tiers.
- [Beam's pricing page](https://www.beam.cloud/pricing) has the on-demand and serverless rates.
- [getdeploying's RTX 4090 tracker](https://getdeploying.com/gpus/nvidia-rtx-4090) supplies the median.


## RTX 4090 marketplace floors vs fixed-rate listings


The cheapest RTX 4090s come from marketplaces and consumer hardware. On Vast.ai, hosts set their own prices, and only one offer in ten costs $0.40 or less. Salad runs on consumer PCs: its High priority tier is never preempted by other workloads, but a node can still disconnect (Salad reallocates the workload automatically), and cheaper tiers can be preempted. That suits retry-safe inference more than long training runs. Fixed-rate listings run from $0.33 (Salad High priority) to $0.74 (RunPod Secure Cloud).


## Where to rent an RTX 4090 for less


Three listings undercut Beam's $0.44: Vast.ai from $0.20, Salad at $0.33, and RunPod Community Cloud at $0.34. Salad and RunPod include vCPU and RAM, and getdeploying shows both in stock. If the lowest hourly rate matters most, start there.


Beam's price buys a fixed rate with NVMe included and a serverless option. Serverless has the higher GPU rate ($0.69 against $0.44) plus CPU and RAM charges, so it only saves money when a GPU would otherwise sit idle for long stretches.


## What this means for your workload


The RTX 4090 handles inference and image generation for models that fit in 24 GB. Retry-safe requests suit marketplace and interruptible capacity. Bursty traffic suits serverless, as long as you plan for[cold starts on serverless GPUs](https://www.beam.cloud/blog/cold-start-serverless-gpu-inference) after idle stretches. Steady, round-the-clock serving belongs on a fixed-rate machine. If you need more memory, the[RTX 5090 has 32 GB](https://www.beam.cloud/blog/nvidia-rtx-5090-pricing) at a $0.64 median. Weighing a purchase instead? Our[RTX 4090 price guide](https://www.beam.cloud/blog/rtx-4090-price) covers what the card costs to buy.


## FAQ


### How much does an RTX 4090 cost per hour?


It costs $0.20 to $0.44 per GPU-hour on demand across the providers above, with a market median of $0.47 across 14 providers. Beam's machine is $0.44 an hour, and its serverless 4090 is $0.69 an hour for the GPU on every plan.


### What's the cheapest way to rent an RTX 4090?


Vast.ai's marketplace starts at $0.20, but its median offer is $0.48. If your job can be preempted, Salad's interruptible tiers start at $0.16. The cheapest fixed rates here are Salad High priority ($0.33) and RunPod Community Cloud ($0.34).


### RTX 4090 vs RTX 5090: which should I rent?


Rent the 4090 if your model fits in 24 GB; its median is $0.47 against $0.64 for the 5090. Pay for the 5090 when you need 32 GB. On Beam, the machines cost $0.44 and $0.72 an hour.
